title: How to use ChatGPT to analyze sales data: an Excel and Sheets practice lab
summary: Clean a messy sales CSV with ChatGPT, preserve refunds, resolve a missing cost, verify the figures in Excel or Google Sheets, and write a checked business memo. Includes original data, a formula workbook, chart and answer key.
label: AI sales-analysis lab
intro: A complete hands-on project with a dirty sales export, four staged prompts, independent calculations and an observable completion rubric.
audience: Small teams responsible for sales reporting

estimatedMinutes.basis: Editorial planning estimate, not measured learner completion time.

prerequisites: Open a CSV in Excel or Google Sheets.
Enter and copy a basic formula.
Use an account with the required ChatGPT analysis/file tools, or follow the spreadsheet-only verification route.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish an event key from an order key.
Write and apply explicit cleaning rules without deleting legitimate refunds.
Preserve unknown costs until a documented correction resolves them.
Independently reconcile totals and test a missing-cost formula guard.
Produce a chart and business memo whose claims remain within the supplied evidence.

contents.title: Your assignment: explain what September sales actually contributed.
Start with file upload. A paid AI plan is not a prerequisite.
One row is an event, not necessarily a new order.
Ask for a profile and an exception list.
Remove duplicate events. Keep the refund history.
Rebuild the totals in Excel or Google Sheets.
The checked answer is $702 in net sales and $240.90 in contribution.
Build one useful chart, then write a memo that respects the evidence.
If your result differs, trace the difference to a rule.
Assess the finished work against observable requirements.

releaseChecks: The 27-row starter CSV and every referenced exercise file download successfully.
The dictionary distinguishes event-level amounts, refunds, missing costs and genuine zeros.
All four staged prompts are complete and their copy buttons target unique preformatted blocks.
The documented cleaning path retains 23 events and all three refunds.
Net sales reconcile to 702.00 USD and operational contribution to 240.90 USD.
The XLSX formula model recalculates when the confirmed cost is blank, zero or changed.
The chart matches the four checked channel/product values and uses a zero baseline.
The memo identifies omitted costs, sample size and the data required before changing channel strategy.
Vendor screenshots carry local assets, source links and explicit vendor-example captions.
No live-account test, accreditation, verified keyword volume or learner outcome is invented.
readinessItems: Original synthetic data and a field dictionary are available.
An unresolved input must be handled before contribution is complete.
The answer key can be independently reproduced.
The exercise includes a completed chart and evidence-limited memo.
Failure diagnosis maps wrong results to specific data or formula issues.
A completion rubric assesses both arithmetic and business judgment.
Current vendor access instructions distinguish uploads from optional add-ins.

limitations: No accredited course or third-party assessment is claimed.
No controlled learner outcomes have been measured.
Workbook verification used the authoring calculation engine, not a native Excel or Google Sheets UI session.

passCriteria: Retain 23 events, including three refunds, after removing only two exact duplicate rows and two cancelled drafts.
Match 702.00 USD net sales and 240.90 USD contribution to the cent after the documented cost correction.
Demonstrate unknown/zero/changed-cost behavior and write a memo that identifies missing evidence without causal, forecast or final-profit claims.
